text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) usually has no symptoms, which is why doctors call it a "silent killer".

list.snippet: No warning signs: Most people with high blood pressure feel completely fine and do not notice any changes.
The only way to know: You must check your blood pressure with a monitor at a clinic, pharmacy, or at home.

text_blocks.snippet: When blood pressure rises to dangerously high levels—usually above 180/120 mm Hg—it can cause a medical emergency. Seek emergency care immediately if high numbers are paired with these signs:

list.snippet: Severe headache: A sudden, very intense, and throbbing pain.
Chest pain: Tightness or squeezing in the chest.
Shortness of breath: Trouble catching your breath while resting or doing light tasks.
Vision changes: Blurry vision, double vision, or sudden vision loss.
Neurological signs: Sudden confusion, dizziness, trouble speaking, numbness, or weakness.
